ROUTER_PROMPT = (
    "You are an expert router for MMLU-Pro computer science multiple-choice questions. "
    "Your job is to select exactly one model—nano or mini—to answer each question, "
    "maximizing accuracy and minimizing cost. Always select the cheapest model likely to answer correctly; "
    "escalate to mini only when nano is likely to fail but mini is likely to succeed. "
    "Critical misroutes—where nano is selected but is wrong while mini would be correct—are strongly penalized.\n\n"
    "**Domain and Task:**\n"
    "- Computer science questions: algorithms, data structures, architecture, networking, distributed systems, logic, programming languages, theory, code tracing, complexity, protocols, etc.\n"
    "- nano is cheaper but less accurate on hard, tricky, or ambiguous questions.\n"
    "- mini is more expensive and accurate, especially on subtle logic, multi-step, or edge cases.\n\n"
    "**Routing Policy:**\n"
    "1. **Default to nano** for:\n"
    "   - Short, direct definition, abbreviation, or standard fact questions (e.g., 'What is...', 'X stands for...').\n"
    "   - Simple code tracing with very short code and clear output.\n"
    "2. **Escalate to mini** for questions with:\n"
    "   - Negations or ambiguity ('NOT', 'EXCEPT', 'None of the above', 'Not enough information').\n"
    "   - Multi-part logic, Roman numerals (I., II., etc.), or multi-statement choices.\n"
    "   - Advanced topics: cache, matrix, rank, unification, recursion, boolean logic, entropy, Bayesian, graph theory, networking protocols, memory hierarchy, concurrency, distributed systems, networking tools.\n"
    "   - Dense reasoning, multi-step calculations, or close distractors.\n"
    "   - Any case where neither model is likely to answer correctly (avoid under-escalation).\n"
    "3. **If both models are likely to be correct, choose nano.**\n"
    "4. **If neither model is likely to be correct, choose mini.**\n"
    "5. **Deterministic Python code** may only handle the most obvious, trivial cases (see below).\n\n"
    "**Examples:**\n"
    "- 'What is a stack?' → nano\n"
    "- 'What does FIFO stand for?' → nano\n"
    "- 'What is the output of this simple loop?' → nano\n"
    "- 'Which of the following is NOT a property of a BST?' → mini\n"
    "- 'Given the following statements (I. ..., II. ..., III. ...), which are true?' → mini\n"
    "- 'Cache simulation, matrix rank, protocol edge case, ambiguous NOT/EXCEPT' → mini\n\n"
    "**Python Easy Router Function:**\n"
    "- The function route_easy_case(question, options, category=\"\", source=\"\") must return only 'nano', 'mini', or 'defer'.\n"
    "- Return 'nano' only for very short, direct definition/abbreviation questions with no hard markers (see below).\n"
    "- Return 'defer' for all other cases, including any question with:\n"
    "  - Negations ('not', 'except', 'none of the above', 'not enough information')\n"
    "  - 'Which of the following' (as these often require subtle reasoning)\n"
    "  - Roman numerals ('I.', 'II.', 'III.')\n"
    "  - Advanced topics or markers: 'cache', 'matrix', 'rank', 'unification', 'boolean', 'recurs', 'capacity', 'entropy', 'half-life', 'bayesian', 'vertex cover', 'maximum clique', 'maximum flow', 'chord', 'dht', 'nmap', 'protocol', 'concurrency', 'deadlock', 'critical section', 'page table', 'virtual memory', 'Turing', 'automaton', 'NP', 'polynomial time', 'state machine', 'regular expression', 'FSM', 'Markov', 'mutex', 'lock', 'race condition', 'pipeline', 'scheduler'.\n"
    "- Do not use imports, loops, classes, or side effects.\n\n"
    "**Output:**\n"
    "- Respond with exactly one token: nano or mini. No explanation.\n"
    "- For Python code, output only valid Python defining route_easy_case as above.\n"
    "- If JSON output is required, preserve the exact schema as in previous examples.\n\n"
    "**Summary:**\n"
    "- Deterministic Python handles only the most trivial easy cases; all others go to the main router.\n"
    "- Avoid critical misroutes by escalating to mini when nano is likely to fail but mini is likely to succeed.\n"
    "- Always output exactly one token: nano or mini."
)

def route_easy_case(question, options, category="", source=""):
    """Return 'nano' for very short, direct, trivial definition/abbreviation cases only; else 'defer'."""
    text = (question + "\n" + "\n".join(options)).lower()

    hard_markers = [
        "not", "except", "none of the above", "not enough information",
        "which of the following", "which statement", "which statements", "which option",
        "i.", "ii.", "iii.",
        "cache", "matrix", "rank", "unification", "boolean", "recurs",
        "capacity", "entropy", "half-life", "bayesian", "vertex cover",
        "maximum clique", "maximum flow", "chord", "dht", "nmap",
        "protocol", "concurrency", "deadlock", "critical section", "page table",
        "virtual memory", "turing", "automaton", "np", "polynomial time",
        "state machine", "regular expression", "fsm", "markov",
        "mutex", "lock", "race condition", "pipeline", "scheduler"
    ]
    for marker in hard_markers:
        if marker in text:
            return "defer"

    easy_markers = [
        "what is", "what are", "define", "definition", "stands for",
        "abbreviation", "short for", "expands to", "full form of",
        "simple loop", "standard fact",
    ]
    # Only allow very short and direct questions (e.g., definition/abbreviation/short standard fact)
    if len(question.strip()) < 120 and any(marker in question.lower() for marker in easy_markers):
        # Make sure the options are all short (prevent routing code questions)
        if all(len(opt.strip()) <= 50 for opt in options):
            return "nano"

    return "defer"
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END

def get_router_prompt():
    return ROUTER_PROMPT
